quiz_met2:1.q: A resting patient's brain consumes ATP at a steady rate whether he is asleep or awake. Which process does this constant ATP use drive?
quiz_met2:1.r: The brain's constitutive energy use goes to electrogenic transport by the Na+K+ ATPase (p. 619), which is how it transports ions to maintain membrane potential (p. 617). Mechanical work is muscle, urea is liver, and heat is brown fat.

quiz_met2:10.q: After a meal, glucose enters a pancreatic beta cell through GLUT2 and is oxidized, raising ATP. What is the direct effect of this rise in ATP on the beta cell membrane?
o: Moves GLUT4 to the cell surface
quiz_met2:10.r: Raised ATP closes the ATP-gated K+ channel; the membrane then depolarizes, voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open, Ca2+ rises and insulin granules are secreted (p. 628). The Ca2+ channel opens because of depolarization, one step later.

quiz_met2:11.q: An experimental hormone infusion increases glycogen breakdown in both liver and skeletal muscle and lowers insulin secretion. Which hormone was infused?
quiz_met2:11.r: Epinephrine raises glycogen breakdown in muscle and liver and lowers insulin secretion (p. 636). Glucagon's glycogen breakdown is listed for liver only (p. 631), and the summary table shows no muscle effect for it (p. 638).

quiz_met2:12.q: A man with type 2 diabetes and constant hunger starts a drug that mimics an incretin known to slow gastric emptying. Which cells are the main natural source of this hormone?
quiz_met2:12.r: GLP-1 is the incretin that also slows gastric emptying, and it is released primarily by L cells in the ileum, and also by the colon (p. 642). Her slides spell it 'ilium', so pick that spelling on her exam; the pancreas is its target, not its source.

quiz_met2:13.q: An ob/ob mouse is massively obese because it cannot make one hormone. In its normal littermate, which tissue secretes that hormone?
quiz_met2:13.r: The ob/ob mouse is leptin deficient (p. 612), and leptin is secreted by adipose tissue and travels via blood to the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (p. 640). The arcuate nucleus is leptin's target, not its source.

quiz_met2:14.q: A hungry patient's arcuate nucleus receives a hormonal signal that results in the output to eat more and metabolize less. Which hormone and action produce this output?
quiz_met2:14.r: Ghrelin from the stomach stimulates the orexigenic (NPY) neurons, whose message is 'eat more; metabolize less' (p. 641). Leptin, insulin and PYY3-36 all inhibit the NPY neurons, and leptin and insulin stimulate the anorexigenic (alpha-MSH) neurons.

quiz_met2:15.q: A patient with obesity and high blood glucose starts a drug that mimics GLP-1. Which set of effects is expected?
o: More appetite, more insulin, less glucagon
Less appetite, less insulin, more glucagon
Less appetite, more insulin, more glucagon
Less appetite, more insulin, less glucagon
More appetite, less insulin, more glucagon
quiz_met2:15.r: GLP-1 lowers appetite and raises satiety in the brain, and in the pancreas it raises insulin and lowers glucagon (p. 642). The review slide says it helps control high blood glucose by increasing insulin release and inhibiting glucagon release (p. 643).

quiz_met2:2.q: A mature red blood cell and a neuron are each supplied with glucose and ample oxygen. What does the red blood cell make from glucose, and why?
o: Lactate, as oxygen is too scarce
CO2 and H2O, as it carries oxygen
CO2 and H2O, as it has mitochondria
Ketone bodies, as it lacks a nucleus
quiz_met2:2.r: Red blood cells carry out anaerobic catabolism, converting pyruvate to lactate, because they lack mitochondria, the location of oxidative phosphorylation (p. 616). The brain is the tissue that burns glucose aerobically to CO2 and H2O.

quiz_met2:3.q: During a fast, a patient's white adipocytes release glycerol and fatty acids into nearby capillaries. Which enzyme cleaves the stored triglyceride inside the fat cell?
quiz_met2:3.r: Hormone-sensitive lipase cleaves the stored triglyceride to glycerol and fatty acids inside the fat cell (p. 621). Lipoprotein lipase works within the capillary, on chylomicrons and VLDL.

quiz_met2:4.q: Cold exposure triggers norepinephrine release onto a brown adipocyte, and a lipase frees fatty acids from its triglyceride. Unlike in a white adipocyte, what is the main fate of these fatty acids?
o: Export to blood bound to albumin
Conversion to ketone bodies for the brain
Conversion to glucose for the brain
Packaging into VLDL for the liver
quiz_met2:4.r: In brown fat the freed fatty acids undergo beta-oxidation in the cell's own mitochondria, and the uncoupling protein (thermogenin, UCP1) turns the proton gradient into heat (p. 622). White fat instead sends its fatty acids into blood on albumin (p. 621).

quiz_met2:5.q: After an overnight fast, glucagon shifts a patient's liver into its glucogenic state. Which pair of fuels does this liver generate for other tissues?
quiz_met2:5.r: The glucogenic liver generates glucose and ketone bodies during the fasting state under glucagon and epinephrine (p. 643, drawn on p. 635). Fatty acids and glycogen are the products of the lipogenic liver under insulin.

quiz_met2:6.q: A man fasts for three days, and his liver keeps making glucose from carbon sent by adipose tissue and muscle. Which pairing gives the gluconeogenic substrate supplied by each tissue?
o: Adipose fatty acids, muscle amino acids
quiz_met2:6.r: In the fasting state, adipose triacylglycerol sends glycerol into gluconeogenesis and muscle protein sends amino acids (p. 635; Table 23-4 on p. 631 lists amino acids and glycerol). The fatty acids go to ketone bodies and ATP, not to glucose.

quiz_met2:7.q: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, a patient's liver converts excess glucose to triacylglycerol under the influence of insulin. In what form does this lipid travel from the liver to adipose tissue?
quiz_met2:7.r: In the well-fed (lipogenic) liver, glucose goes to pyruvate, acetyl-CoA and then triacylglycerol, which leaves as VLDL for storage in adipose tissue (p. 630). Dietary fat, not liver fat, travels through the lymphatic system.

quiz_met2:8.q: During an acute stress response, epinephrine stimulates glycogen breakdown in skeletal muscle. In what form does this muscle carbon reach the liver for conversion to glucose?
quiz_met2:8.r: In the stressed state, epinephrine drives muscle glycogen to pyruvate and lactate, which travel to the liver and become glucose (p. 637). Glycerol and fatty acids come from adipose tissue, not muscle.

quiz_met2:9.q: A healthy volunteer eats a high-protein meal, and serum hormones are measured over the next two hours. How do insulin and glucagon change?
quiz_met2:9.r: A high-protein meal raises both insulin and glucagon while blood glucose stays flat (p. 634); raised amino acids stimulate the alpha cells (p. 633). A high-carbohydrate meal is the one that raises insulin and lowers glucagon.

quiz_met2_b:1.q: A sprinter's muscle converts pyruvate to lactate during an all-out effort. According to the lecture, what does this conversion accomplish?
o: Regenerates NAD+ when O2 is scarce
Supplies ketone bodies to the brain
quiz_met2_b:1.r: Muscle can catabolize glucose aerobically or anaerobically; conversion of pyruvate to lactate allows regeneration of NAD+ when O2 is scarce, as during intense exercise (p. 616). Releasing glucose into blood is the liver's job.

quiz_met2_b:10.q: Shortly after a carbohydrate meal, while insulin is high, a patient receives an epinephrine injection for anaphylaxis. According to the lecture, what happens to his blood glucose?
o: Unchanged, as the two effects cancel
quiz_met2_b:10.r: Epinephrine can counteract the effects of insulin and will lead to increased blood glucose even when insulin is present (p. 637). On the same slide epinephrine raises glucagon from the alpha cell and lowers insulin from the beta cell.

quiz_met2_b:11.q: Liver takes up glucose through an insulin-independent transporter, yet insulin still raises hepatic glucose uptake. According to the lecture, which target does insulin increase to do this?
quiz_met2_b:11.r: Table 23-3 lists increased glucose uptake in muscle and adipose through GLUT4, but in liver through glucokinase (increased expression) (p. 626). Liver uses Glut2, which is insulin independent (p. 627).

quiz_met2_b:12.q: A lean mouse is infused with leptin, which signals through the hypothalamus and sympathetic neurons back to adipose tissue. According to the lecture, how do fat synthesis and fat beta oxidation change?
quiz_met2_b:12.r: Leptin from adipose tissue travels via blood to the arcuate nucleus, and the neuronal signal returns via a sympathetic neuron; the slide marks fat synthesis as inhibited and fat beta oxidation as stimulated, giving energy and heat (p. 640).

quiz_met2_b:13.q: After surgery removes most of a patient's stomach, his hunger drops sharply. According to the lecture, the main source of which hormone was removed?
quiz_met2_b:13.r: Ghrelin comes from the stomach and stimulates the orexigenic (NPY) neurons (p. 641); the review slide calls ghrelin orexigenic (p. 643). Leptin comes from adipose tissue, insulin from the pancreas, PYY3-36 from the colon and GLP-1 from the 'ilium'.

quiz_met2_b:14.q: An ob/ob mouse cannot make leptin. According to the lecture, how does this change the activity of the NPY and alpha-MSH neurons of its arcuate nucleus?
o: NPY neurons down, alpha-MSH neurons up
NPY neurons up, alpha-MSH neurons down
quiz_met2_b:14.r: Leptin inhibits the orexigenic (NPY) neurons and stimulates the anorexigenic (alpha-MSH) neurons (p. 641). Without leptin (the ob/ob mouse, p. 612) the NPY neurons lose their brake and the alpha-MSH neurons lose their drive, so the message is 'eat more; metabolize less'.

quiz_met2_b:15.q: A peptide released by the colon acts directly on the orexigenic neurons of the arcuate nucleus. According to the lecture, which hormone is it and what is its effect on those neurons?
quiz_met2_b:15.r: PYY3-36 is drawn leaving the colon and inhibiting the orexigenic (NPY) neuron through its own receptor (p. 641). Ghrelin, from the stomach, is the only hormone drawn stimulating that neuron.

quiz_met2_b:2.q: A patient who injected too much insulin has blood glucose falling steadily below the normal range. According to the lecture's scale, which of these appears first?
quiz_met2_b:2.r: Reading down the brain's blood glucose scale: subtle neurological signs and hunger come first (about 60 mg/100 mL), then release of glucagon, epinephrine and cortisol, sweating and trembling, lethargy, convulsions and coma, permanent brain damage and death (p. 619).

quiz_met2_b:3.q: In a brown adipocyte's mitochondria, H+ pumped by the electron transport chain re-enters the matrix through thermogenin instead of Fo F1. What is the result?
o: ATP is made from ADP and Pi
Heat is released instead of ATP
quiz_met2_b:3.r: H+ returning through Fo F1 makes ATP from ADP and Pi, while H+ returning through the uncoupling protein (thermogenin, UCP1) releases the gradient's energy as heat (p. 622). That is why brown fat carries out thermogenesis (p. 617).

quiz_met2_b:4.q: After a meal, a white adipocyte re-forms triglyceride from fatty acids freed by lipoprotein lipase in the capillary. According to the lecture, from what does the fat cell make the glycerol phosphate it needs?
quiz_met2_b:4.r: On the white fat slide, glucose from the capillary becomes glycerol phosphate in the fat cell, which joins free fatty acids to form the stored triglyceride (p. 621). Glycerol is drawn only leaving the fat cell, after hormone-sensitive lipase acts.

quiz_met2_b:5.q: A hepatocyte must make ATP for itself in both the well-fed and the fasting state. According to the lecture, which fuel does the liver oxidize for its own ATP in each state?
o: Fed: fatty acids; fasting: ketone bodies
quiz_met2_b:5.r: In the well-fed (lipogenic) liver, glucose goes to pyruvate and acetyl-CoA, which yields ATP and CO2 (p. 630). In the fasting (glucogenic) liver, fatty acids from adipose tissue yield the ATP and CO2, while glucose and ketone bodies are exported (p. 635).

quiz_met2_b:6.q: During an overnight fast, the liver releases glucose made from both glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis. According to the lecture, on which intermediate do both routes converge just before free glucose?
quiz_met2_b:6.r: In the fasting liver, glycogen and gluconeogenesis (from pyruvate and from glycerol) both feed glucose 6-phosphate, which becomes glucose and is exported to the brain (p. 635).

quiz_met2_b:7.q: On the third day of a fast, a patient's liver converts fatty acids from adipose tissue into ketone bodies. According to the lecture, which tissues receive and burn them?
quiz_met2_b:7.r: The fasting-state drawing sends ketone bodies from the liver to the brain and to muscle, where each burns them to ATP and CO2 (p. 635). Red blood cells lack mitochondria and can only make lactate from glucose (p. 616).

quiz_met2_b:8.q: One liver enzyme is raised by insulin to drive fatty acid synthesis and lowered by glucagon to favor ketogenesis. Which enzyme is it?
quiz_met2_b:8.r: Insulin raises acetyl-CoA carboxylase for fatty acid synthesis in the liver (Table 23-3, p. 626), and glucagon lowers acetyl-CoA carboxylase, listed beside increased ketogenesis (Table 23-4, p. 631). This one enzyme marks the switch between lipogenic and glucogenic liver.

quiz_met2_b:9.q: A patient with untreated type 1 diabetes makes no insulin. According to the lecture, which pair of tissues loses its glucose transport because their transporter works only after insulin is released?
quiz_met2_b:9.r: Glut4 (fatty tissue, skeletal muscle, heart) is insulin dependent and only transports glucose after insulin is released; Glut1 (erythrocytes), Glut2 (liver, pancreatic beta cells, intestine) and Glut3 (brain) are insulin independent, and Glut5 (jejunum, kidney) is the fructose transporter (p. 627).

Met 2: Integration of Mammalian Metabolism and Division of Metabolic Labor (Jones). Your September first attempt was 24/32.
